title: Morning Headlines
intro: SpaceX makes history on Wall Street as geopolitical and economic tremors reverberate worldwide — from an unresolved Iran war ceasefire claim to a fresh World Bank growth alarm.

items.title: SpaceX Begins Nasdaq Trading in Record-Breaking $75 Billion IPO
items.subtitle: NPR / Bloomberg / Axios
items.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX priced 555 million shares at $135 each, raising $75 billion — nearly three times Saudi Aramco's 2019 record — and began trading today under ticker SPCX at a $1.75 trillion valuation. The listing is the first of a trio of anticipated AI mega-IPOs, with OpenAI and Anthropic also having filed SEC paperwork for their own debuts.

items.title: Trump Claims Iran War Has Ended; Tehran Disputes Any Final Deal
items.subtitle: Axios / Sunday Guardian Live
items.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social that 'the war with Iran has ended today' and that Iran agreed never to pursue a nuclear weapon, suggesting a signing ceremony in Europe is imminent. Iran's foreign ministry denied any finalized agreement, calling reports 'speculative,' leaving the status of a reported 60-day memorandum of understanding unresolved.

items.title: World Bank Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast to Post-Pandemic Low of 2.5%
items.subtitle: Reuters / Investing.com
items.summary: The World Bank slashed its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.5% — the weakest since the COVID pandemic — citing energy price spikes and financial stress caused by the Iran war. In a severe downside scenario the bank warned growth could collapse to 1.3%, with developing economies and the Middle East region hit hardest.

items.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Kicks Off Across North America
items.subtitle: ESPN
items.summary: The most-watched sporting event in history opened on June 11 with matches spread across 16 cities in the United States, Mexico, and Canada — the first World Cup jointly hosted by three nations. Mexico defeated South Africa 2-0 in the tournament opener, with South Korea also claiming a win on day one.

items.title: Second Night of Anti-Immigrant Violence Erupts in Belfast
items.subtitle: Morning Star / Foreign Exchanges
items.summary: Protesters set fires and hurled bricks and bottles at police in Belfast for a second consecutive night after a stabbing triggered a wave of anti-immigrant unrest in Northern Ireland. The riots drew comparisons to the 2024 Southport riots in England and have raised alarm about the spread of far-right mobilisation across the UK.
